transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-09-14
Start time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Martinez (Redwood AE), Sam Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Orion CTO), Miguel Santos (Infra Lead), Dana Lee (Security), Ethan Park (ML Eng)

Summary: quick discovery focused on Private/VPC deployment requirements, networking (VPC peering, private endpoints), region constraints (EU data residency), and integration with Orion's existing transit gateway and SSO/KMS needs. Agreed action items and next steps at end.

[00:00] Alex (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're gonna do a 30-45 minute discovery on private deployment options for Redwood, specifically VPC setup, peering, private endpoints, stuff like that. quick intros?
[00:12] Priya (CTO): sure hi, I'm Priya, CTO at Orion. we're evaluating options for model inference for our customer-facing features, need to keep data in eu-west-1 and meet SOC2-ish controls.
[00:25] Miguel (Infra): miguel here, infra lead, mostly networking and infra constraints, we run transit-gw and use VPC peering for some partners.
[00:32] Alex (AE): cool, Sam do you wanna intro?
[00:35] Sam (SE): yeah hey all, Sam Chen, se focusing on private deployment and perf, i'll cover architecture, network patterns, things to watch for with KV cache and GPU nodes.
[00:44] Ethan (ML Eng): ethan, ML eng, interested in latency targets, throughput and model versions we can pin.

[01:05] Alex (AE): quick qual — what's your timeline and success criteria for this?
[01:10] Priya (CTO): timeline is Q4 pilot, production early Q1 if things look good. success is sub-200ms p95 for single-turn prompt in eu-west-1 for our smaller models, and predictably scaling to handle spikes during peak hours. also we need audit logs and key management.

[01:40] Sam (SE): ok noted. on the networking side we support three private deployment patterns: 1) VPC peering to Redwood-managed VPC, 2) PrivateEndpoint with interface endpoints (we can deploy endpoints into your VPC), or 3) fully customer-managed private nodes in your account (on-prem or customer cloud accounts) — each has tradeoffs around maintenance, egress, and latency.
[02:10] Miguel (Infra): can you clarify the difference between the peering and private endpoint? we use a transit-gw hub, peering sometimes gets messy with route limits.
[02:22] Sam (SE): yeah with VPC peering we establish a peer between your VPC and Redwood's service VPC; it's simple but does require route table entries both ways and can hit route limits on large architectures. For transit-gw, we can peer to a service VPC that then attaches to transit-gw, but you may prefer endpoint approach — interface endpoints use ENIs in your subnet and traffic stays within your account, so easier for egress control and no peering routes.
[02:55] Dana (Security): do you support AWS PrivateLink? that's what our security team prefers for controlled egress.
[03:02] Sam (SE): yep PrivateLink is our interface endpoint offering — we can publish a network interface into your VPC and you get an endpoint DNS name. That keeps traffic internal and avoids exposing public IPs.
[03:14] Miguel (Infra): what's the egress story? we need all outbound to go through our NAT and egress inspection tools.
[03:20] Sam (SE): with interface endpoints traffic egress remains inside your VPC, so your NAT and inspection still apply for anything that leaves to other services. if we do peering to our VPC, egress from Redwood-run nodes will leave via Redwood's egress unless you choose a customer-managed node option. For tight egress control, customer-managed nodes or endpoints are recommended.

[03:45] Priya (CTO): region constraint — we must keep data residency in eu-west-1. can Redwood run entirely in eu-west-1?
[03:52] Alex (AE): yes, we can deploy private plane in specific regions. For Dedicated we can provision capacity in eu-west-1; for Private on-prem we can run in your cloud account in eu-west-1. There are options to pin model versions and control failover behavior.
[04:12] Ethan (ML Eng): if we run in eu-west-1 what about peak capacity? do you support bursting to other regions and still keep data in eu-west-1?
[04:20] Sam (SE): we try to avoid cross-region bursting for private deployments because of data residency. For hosted we can route workloads to nearby regions; for private/vpc we can set policy to deny cross-region fallbacks. If you need occasional bursting, we'd discuss data masking or approval flows, but generally we keep compute in region.

[04:50] Miguel (Infra): IP addressing — do you need public IPs on the Redwood nodes? Our security wants no public IPs.
[04:57] Sam (SE): no public IPs required. For interface endpoints and customer-managed nodes, we can keep everything private. For Redwood-managed VPC peering we typically do not require nodes to have public IPs; outbound traffic is managed by our egress setup, but if you need no public IPs at all, customer-managed deployment is the safest.

[05:30] Dana (Security): key management — can we bring our own KMS? we need CMKs for encryption at rest and audit of key usage.
[05:38] Alex (AE): yes Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) is supported in Private deployments. We'll integrate with your AWS KMS or HSM depending on the pattern. We'll surface audit logs to your SIEM. Sam will follow up with exact integration docs.

[06:05] Priya (CTO): curious about SSO and RBAC — we use SAML okta and need role-based access for operators and devs.
[06:14] Sam (SE): Redwood Console can integrate with SAML/SSO and we support granular RBAC and logging. For private deployments we can federate to your identity provider so operators use existing roles.

[06:35] Alex (AE): curious competitors or alternatives you're evaluating?
[06:39] Priya (CTO): looking at Anthropic and also considering a self-hosted stack; compliance and cost are main tiebreakers.

[06:48] Sam (SE): ok good to know. we'll include a comparison sheet.

[07:05] Ethan (ML Eng): performance question — for multi-turn chat we rely heavily on KV cache, does the private deployment expose same KV cache speed?
[07:14] Sam (SE): yes, same runtime with KV cache locality. Key is network latency between the app tier and the inference nodes. If you colocate inference in the same VPC/subnets as the app or route via internal network we see best p95. Also we can co-locate a small set of frontends in your VPC to minimize hop count.

[07:40] Miguel (Infra): any special ports or firewall rules we need to open?
[07:44] Sam (SE): typically we need to allow outbound to the endpoint IPs on TCP 443 if using interface endpoints; for peering we need those VPC CIDR ranges and health-check endpoints for load balancers (we'll provide a list). If you run in your account, fewer external rules. We'll share a checklist.

[08:10] Priya (CTO): logging and audit retention — we need 1 year of audit logs for compliance.
[08:16] Alex (AE): Redwood can stream logs to your CloudWatch/S3 or SIEM; retention policies are configurable as an add-on if you need longer retention. We'll include options and pricing.

[08:44] Dana (Security): penetration testing — can we perform our pen test on the private deployment?
[08:50] Sam (SE): yes, with coordination; if it's customer-managed nodes you can test as you like. For Redwood-managed service we have a limited scope and need a permit, but we can provide a process and schedule.

[09:10] Miguel (Infra): what about VPC CIDR conflicts? we have many /16s reserved and sometimes peering hits overlap.
[09:17] Sam (SE): CIDR overlap is a blocker for peering. For endpoint approach that's not an issue. For peering, we can also use a proxy VPC or ask you to carve a /20 for the connected subnets. If you're using transit-gw, we can attach via a service VPC to avoid direct peering into many accounts.

[09:45] Ethan (ML Eng): can we pin specific model versions and quantization profiles per route?
[09:51] Sam (SE): yes, per-route model pinning and quantization profiles are supported. That way you can route high-quality models for critical paths and lower-cost quantized ones for high-throughput internal tasks.

[10:12] Alex (AE): cost question — is there an upfront footprint or reserved capacity?
[10:18] Sam (SE): for Dedicated private capacity we have reserved commit (monthly) and you can provision a baseline with burst options. For private in your account, pricing is different — usually a platform/license plus usage. We'll produce a sizing + cost snapshot.

[10:40] Miguel (Infra): do you support GCP and Azure as well or just AWS?
[10:44] Sam (SE): we support AWS, GCP, and Azure for private deployments. Some features (like specific managed KMS integrations) vary by cloud. Since you're on AWS, we'll focus on AWS docs.

[11:05] Priya (CTO): network egress IPs — our allowlist only accepts static egress IPs. how do you handle that?
[11:13] Sam (SE): we can allocate static egress IPs for outbound calls; if you want everything to appear from your NAT, the customer-managed nodes pattern is ideal. For Redwood-managed endpoints we can provide a range of IPs and update you. We'll include the IP list in the security pack.

[11:38] Dana (Security): data in transit encryption and mTLS?
[11:43] Sam (SE): TLS is standard; mutual TLS can be configured for additional assurance on some private endpoint patterns. We'll include mTLS details.

[12:05] Ethan (ML Eng): any constraints around GPU types / model quantization?
[12:11] Sam (SE): we run on a variety of GPU types and support quantized runtimes. For private we can recommend instance families in eu-west-1 that match your latency/cost targets. We'll run bench with your prompt sets.

[12:35] Alex (AE): what's the onboarding path if we want to run a pilot?
[12:39] Sam (SE): typical pilot: 1) share network checklist and minimal permissions, 2) deploy a small private footprint in eu-west-1 (2-3 nodes), 3) run benchmarks and tuning with your prompt set, 4) finalize sizing and roll to production. Usually 3-6 weeks depending on approvals.

[13:05] Priya (CTO): approvals — we'll need a security review; Dana will coordinate.
[13:09] Dana (Security): yes i'll need the architecture diagram, IP list, security pack and SOC2 evidence.

[13:25] Alex (AE): we'll send the security pack and a network checklist after this call. Sam will prepare the sizing and bench plan.

[13:40] Miguel (Infra): one last question — do you support private DNS resolution for endpoints? we use private hosted zones.
[13:46] Sam (SE): yes endpoints are reachable via private DNS entries and we can support private hosted zones or provide CNAMEs that resolve to endpoint ENIs. We'll include DNS guidance.

[14:05] Ethan (ML Eng): are there any gotchas with KV cache persistence across node restarts?
[14:10] Sam (SE): cache warms after restarts; for critical low-latency flows we recommend a stable node pool and pre-warming during deployments. We'll provide pre-warm scripts.

[14:30] Alex (AE): ok let's recap next steps.

End of transcript.

References mentioned: security pack (link to shared doc), network checklist (will be attached), benchmarking spreadsheet (to be shared).
